pairs.reason: A keeps the whole ending inside the room it opened — the washed cup and "Mind how you go" carry the badness without naming it — whereas B turns the same quiet brief into a conspiracy hook its short frame cannot pay.
pairs.strength_A: Prose and emotional credibility are carried by objects rather than adjectives: "the tea gone to a grey skin" does the work a paragraph of grief would have done.
pairs.defect_A: The motive behind his refusal is stated rather than left to the scene — "Ray had enough of that." — one clause of explanation where the ritual had been enough.
pairs.strength_B: Structural integrity is excellent: the bolt thrown at the start returns at the close, "the sound of it was exactly the same", and the ledger's "opened" lands the change.
pairs.defect_B: "You won't say about the bolt." imports a conspiracy the story neither explains nor needs, converting a quietly bad ending into an unresolved thriller beat.

pairs.reason: Both are well made, but B develops all three lines to a real weight and lets one object physically join them, while A stays a compressed sketch whose trial and letter meet only in the final image.
pairs.strength_A: The best sentence in the pair is A's: "Дневник Вера закрыла и положила на кальку" makes the daughter's lie cover the stranger's letter with no commentary at all.
pairs.defect_A: The letter thread stops at its own reveal — "А письма она не просила." — and never touches the trial, so the three lines run parallel to the last page.
pairs.strength_B: The grief is enacted in a posture, not announced: "она держала шапку на коленях, как сумку" tells the reader everything about the sister's rehearsed calm.
pairs.defect_B: The narrator explains what the scene already shows — "не потому, что прятал, а потому, что мёрзли" — against the brief's ban on authorial explanation.

pairs.reason: A never leaves the car park and lets a hedge and an unclaimed fence do all the saying, while B smuggles in a narrator's backstory and a dying-ex-wife twist that 600 words of dialogue-and-action cannot support.
pairs.strength_A: Emotional credibility is exact: the repetition of "It was a good hedge," she said again is disproportionate in the way that reveals her, and the reader is never told what it means.
pairs.defect_A: The box-and-strap logistics take nearly a third of the piece before any pressure exists — "she used to have on a Friday" is doing backstory work the action should carry.
pairs.strength_B: The hospital band is a strong, silent escalation: "white plastic on her wrist, a printed band" raises the stakes without a single line of exposition from either speaker.
pairs.defect_B: The narration keeps explaining the subtext it built — "which he'd said tasted like a hedge" — and the wristband is the modal reveal for this premise rather than a choice of its own.

pairs.reason: A turns the chapter-two hand-off into one continuous argument about a clock, a ledger and a name, while B's eleven-year backdating strains the bible and its own rule that the book holds only refusals.
pairs.strength_A: Character and coherence are the same achievement here: the ledger stops being a grudge and becomes "a kind of memory, which was worse", and every later beat pays off that shift.
pairs.defect_A: The closing line overstates what the scene earned — "Eleven minutes and a woman's whole life in it" — turning a good exit into a caption.
pairs.strength_B: The blank column is handled with real tact: "it had the whole of her in it" makes a thumbnail of white space carry the accusation.
pairs.defect_B: The ninth of October gets a full entry — "The ninth had an entry, all right." — though the bible and B's own description say the book holds only ships he refused.

pairs.reason: B fixes the passage's actual failure — the abstract closing certainty — by replacing it with a concrete fact, whereas A dresses the same cliché in a more careful sentence and calls the revision done.
pairs.strength_A: The middle is genuinely rescued by one observed detail: "crying long enough that she had stopped noticing" is physical, specific, and impossible to move into another story.
pairs.defect_A: The revision leaves the worst sentence standing — "nothing would ever be the same again" — so the passage's real defect survives under a better-lit frame.
pairs.strength_B: The close is the best move in the pair: "She had stood here before, in other weather." converts a declaration into a fact the character knows.
pairs.defect_B: It still reaches for abstraction in the place it claims to have removed it — "the shape of the years" — which its own note says it cut.

pairs.reason: A refuses the speech, refuses the daughter's consolation, and ends on the sentence he cannot forget, while B hands its protagonist the notebook back and so grants a small restitution the brief asked it to withhold.
pairs.strength_A: Originality and character land in the same refusal: the teacher wished him no harm — "это было хуже всего" — and that single judgement declines both catharsis and blame.
pairs.defect_A: The wake's minor figures exist only to cue his silence — "Кто-то кивнул. Виктор Семёнович сказал: «Верно»." — so the room feels staged around him.
pairs.strength_B: The memory is reduced to its true residue: "Он помнил не Ленку, а звук." is precise about what humiliation actually leaves behind.
pairs.defect_B: The flat is inventoried as a list of period properties — "Ковёр на стене, сервант, в серванте хрусталь" — so the setting drifts toward costume rather than evidence.

notes: Word counts checked mechanically. pair-2 A is 992 words against a stated 1400-1800, so brief_ok is false there; that shortfall also shows as under-developed lines, which is the reason the craft scores dip rather than the count itself. pair-1 B is 1103 words against 'around 900' - 23% over, counted as within tolerance for a soft target but noted. pair-6 A is 1601 including its '## 3' heading (1599 body), so counted as compliant. pair-7 revision notes are 94 and 113 words, both inside the 120 limit. pair-4: neither text contains love/hate/sorry/miss; B's narration goes beyond 'the smallest possible amount of action' but that is recorded as a craft defect, not a failed prohibition. Two preferences were close calls: pair-1 (A over B despite B's superior structural closure, because B's conspiracy hook is unpaid) and pair-2 (B over A despite A having the better sentence-level prose, because A's three lines never converge in action). Scores are independent per text; no pair was scored comparatively first.
